definitions.explanation: Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to indicate the beginning of an action. The resulting compound conjugates as an ichidan verb.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めた。
{最近|さいきん}、{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}し{始|はじ}めました。
{桜|さくら}が{咲|さ}き{始|はじ}めると、{公園|こうえん}は{花見|はなみ}の{客|きゃく}でにぎわう。
examples.english: When the cherry blossoms start blooming, the park bustles with hanami visitors.

notes:
FORMS:
Attaches to the masu-stem ({連用形|れんようけい}) of verbs:
- {降|ふ}る → {降|ふ}り + {始|はじ}める → {降|ふ}り{始|はじ}める
- {食|た}べる → {食|た}べ + {始|はじ}める → {食|た}べ{始|はじ}める
- する → し + {始|はじ}める → し{始|はじ}める

The compound conjugates as an ichidan verb ({始|はじ}める).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ～{始|はじ}める vs. ～{出|だ}す: Both mean "to start doing," but ～{出|だ}す implies a more sudden or spontaneous onset. {泣|な}き{出|だ}す (to burst out crying) feels more abrupt than {泣|な}き{始|はじ}める (to start crying). ～{出|だ}す is also used for involuntary actions more naturally.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読|よ}み{始|はじ}める (start reading)
- {走|はし}り{始|はじ}める (start running)
- {使|つか}い{始|はじ}める (start using)
- {動|うご}き{始|はじ}める (start moving)
